turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CAREGIVER): sorry we're late, doc. the parking ramp was shut and she sent me back up for her sweater.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): you're all right. sit wherever's comfortable. i'm dr. hale.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): thanks. umm, my coworker linda's been after me about these stretches off youtube. she had a disc operation last year and she says they'll fix anybody.
[SEG0004] person_4 (NURSE): got her vitals already. blood pressure's one thirty six over eighty two, heart rate's 74, oxygen's ninety eight percent.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): appreciate that. linda aside, what brought you in?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): oh. umm. it's the pain in my lower back. it shoots down my leg.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): which leg are we talking about?
[SEG0008] person_1 (CAREGIVER): she was grabbing the right one the whole ride—
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): yeah, the right leg. it runs down the back of it, kind of burning.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): okay. when did this start?
[SEG0011] person_1 (CAREGIVER): she was gonna say in the car and then she got distracted by—
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): three weeks. it's worse when i sit, like at the register or in the car. standing eases it some. i don't know, doctor, sitting is definitely the bad part.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): any numbness in the foot, any weakness, any trouble peeing or with your bowels?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): no. none of that.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): what have you tried for the pain?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): uh, ibuprophen.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): ibuprofen. what dose, and how often?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): four hundred milligrams three times a day, for the back. i swallow them with water. every day these three weeks, and it takes the edge off.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): any medicine allergies?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): nope. no allergies.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): family side, anybody with diabetes, blood pressure, heart trouble?

[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): umm my father had diabetes in his fifties. my mother did not, no diabetes. my older sister has high blood pressure but no sugar, and my brother had a heart attack when he was sixty.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): what about work, the hours, what you eat, exercise, drinking?

[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): i manage a hardware store. i'm there like eleven hours a day, six days a week. i eat a lot of takeout, burgers mostly, and i don't exercise at all anymore. i'll have two beers on a friday night, and i don't smoke.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): outside the back, any chest pain or shortness of breath?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): no. chest and breathing are fine.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): those long days could be loading the low back. not a diagnosis, just me thinking out loud. ever had surgery on your back?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): no. never.
[SEG0029] person_1 (CAREGIVER): she did try linda's stretches a couple times and they made her yelp, so we quit.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): yeah they pinched. i stopped. i don't know, doctor, if i was even doing them right.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): leave those youtube ones alone. they were aggravating it. lie back for me if you can.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): okay. ow. even getting onto the table.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): i'm going to lift the right leg straight. tell me when it copies your pain.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): there. that's the one. uh.
[SEG0035] person_1 (CAREGIVER): is that bad? she made that face at home too when—

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): one second. straight leg raise on the right is positive at about forty degrees, and the left side goes to around seventy with no pain. tenderness over the right lower lumbar area. ankle strength is good and the reflexes are present.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): so what is it?

[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): i'm not calling it a slipped disc. my working thought is the nerve from the low back is irritated, sciatica, from the pain down the leg and that leg raise. we haven't proven the cause.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): is it serious? i don't know, doctor.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): a lot of these settle with time. i'm going to refer you to physical therapy. i'll put that referral in today so they can book you.
[SEG0041] person_1 (CAREGIVER): and a scan? linda had a scan.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): we might do an mri if it does not settle. i'm not ordering a scan today.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): okay. do i keep the pills?
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): yes, keep the ibuprofen, four hundred milligrams three times a day with food, as long as your stomach's okay with it.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): stomach's been fine, yeah.

[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): don't sit more than twenty or thirty minutes without getting up. short walks are all right. if you suddenly can't pee, or the pain goes into both legs, or the foot gets weak, go to the emergency room.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): got it. umm when do i come back?
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): let's see you back in two weeks. we'll recheck that leg raise and see how the therapy's going.
[SEG0049] person_1 (CAREGIVER): what if they can't fit her in before then?
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): if therapy can't see her first, come anyway. the visit in two weeks stands either way.
[SEG0051] person_4 (NURSE): i can have the front desk book the therapy and the two-week return on the way out.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): please do.
[SEG0053] person_3 (PATIENT): thanks. i still don't know, doctor, whether i slept wrong or what. but okay.

spec.situation: Person with low back pain shooting down one leg for three weeks, worse sitting; takes ibuprofen; a colleague's advice on exercises; doctor examines straight-leg raise and plans physio, no scan yet.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Nurse says front desk can book therapy and return; front desk, not nurse, will book.
bad.text: Front desk to book physical therapy and the two-week return (action_type=other, status=planned, responsible_person=nurse)

omissions.text: Burning quality of the radiating right leg pain running down the back of the leg was stated by the patient.
Ibuprofen only partially relieves symptoms ('takes the edge off').
No medication allergies were reported; recorded fact says 'Allergies' absent rather than specifically medicine allergies.
Back pain worsens even getting onto the exam table.
Left straight leg raise went to around 70 degrees with no pain; the recorded exam omits the approximate angle.
Doctor explicitly said he is not calling this a slipped disc and that the cause has not been proven.
Continue ibuprofen 400 mg three times a day with food only as long as the stomach tolerates it; patient reported stomach has been fine.
Red-flag advice included going to the emergency room if pain goes into both legs.
Follow-up purpose: recheck the straight leg raise and assess how physical therapy is going.
If physical therapy cannot see her before then, she should still come; the two-week follow-up stands either way.
